facts.text: Maren stands about 3 feet 6 inches tall, with a wingspan of roughly 8.5 feet, making her one of the smaller Snowy owl-folk by the standards of her kind.

Her plumage is predominantly white, soft and dense as fresh snow, but her back and wings bear a generous scattering of dark grey markings that form faint patterns resembling drift marks when she spreads her wings.
Her eyes are a striking, vivid blue — unusual among Snowy owl-folk, whose bright yellow eyes are the norm — round and large as they sit forward in her flat facial disc.
A few small nicks and old feather-tears along the leading edges of her left wing testify to years of rough weather and close calls between mountain peaks.

Maren is gregarious to a fault; she finds it nearly impossible to pass through a village without stopping to chat with anyone she encounters, often arriving hours late to her deliveries because she cannot resist asking questions and sharing stories.

She has a habit of tilting her head at extreme angles — sometimes nearly all the way around — while listening, as if trying to catch a sound with both ears at once, which in owl-folk terms is simply how she focuses.
Born in the village of Korrfrost on the northern slopes of the Ashspine Mountains, Maren grew up watching the courier birds arrive and dreamed of flying the routes herself from the age of seven.

She can carry up to six sealed letters in a leather satchel strapped across her chest, tucked between her breast feathers where the wind cannot reach them, and has memorized the major route between a dozen mountain villages along the Ashspine pass.
She has been a licensed courier under the Mountain Guild since the age of fourteen, making her one of the youngest active members on the northern routes.

Her speech is rapid and colorful, peppered with idioms about weather and flight — 'blown in sideways' for arriving out of order, 'talon-deep in it' for being busy — and she tends to narrate her own journey aloud as she walks, which startles other travelers who can hear her chattering from around a bend before they see her.

facts.text: Brennan is a stocky man of five feet seven inches, with broad shoulders and thick forearms built from years of hauling cargo and splitting dice. His skin is a weathered olive-grey, roughened by salt and sun, and his red hair — a trait he owes to some long-lost Lowlander ancestor — is cropped short and perpetually disheveled, sticking up in tufts as though he can never be bothered to tame it. A faint cluster of dark freckles speckles his nose and cheeks, the kind of marking no orcish bloodline could account for.

His eyes are a deep, muddy brown — common enough among quarter-orcs — but his brow ridge sits heavier than most of his kin's, a low shelf of bone that gives his otherwise unremarkable face a perpetual look of suspicion. His tusk buds are barely visible, two tiny nubs on his lower jaw that he's never bothered to file down, though they catch on his lip when he grins.

Born in the port town of Brinewall to a half-orc mother who worked the fish stalls and a Lowlander father who disappeared before Brennan could walk, he grew up in a cramped tenement above the docks and learned to handle a rope before he learned to read. He started hauling crates at fourteen and never stopped, though the work has grown increasingly tedious over the past decade.

He runs an illicit dice game out of the back room of a chandler's shop on Lantern Street, operating under the alias 'Red Bren' and rotating the location every few weeks to stay ahead of the harbor watch. The games are small-time — a few silver per hand, nothing that draws the attention of the local guilds — but his luck at the table has been abysmal for months, and his debts have spiraled out of control.

He owes forty-three silver to Maren Thatch, the chandler whose shop he uses as a front; thirty-one silver to a dock foreman named Gullick, who advanced him wages against future work; and an unspecified but considerable sum to a loan shark operating out of the Mermaid's Keg tavern, the exact number of which Brennan has stopped counting because the interest compounds weekly and the shark's name sounds like a threat when spoken aloud.

Brennan is loud, gregarious, and almost aggressively friendly when he's not stressed, the kind of man who slaps you on the back and buys you a drink before you've exchanged names. But when the debt collectors start circling — and they always start circling — he becomes twitchy and evasive, ducking into alleys, lying to his face when asked where he's been, and muttering to himself in a low grumble that his dockmates have learned to recognize as trouble.

He has a gift for telling stories that makes people forget they came to the table to gamble, spinning tall tales about sea monsters and sunken treasure that keep the dice rolling even after the real game has been rigged in his favor — though lately the rigging has gone sideways, and he suspects someone is marking the dice before he gets to them.

He can break a crate open with his bare hands when the nails come loose, a trick that impresses dockhands and frightens the merchants who hire him. His grip strength is preternatural for a man his size, a lingering gift from his mother's orcish blood that he considers his only useful inheritance.

He speaks with a thick Brinewall accent — the kind that drops consonants and runs words together until strangers need a translator — and has a habit of punctuating his sentences with grunts and clicks of his tongue that his Lowlander coworkers find strange but his quarter-orc neighbors take for granted. When he's angry or desperate, his voice drops to a rumble that sounds more orcish than he'd like to admit.

He has not missed a single day of dock work in six years, even when he was sick with the harbor fever that swept Brinewall in 809, because the foreman docks pay for missed days and he cannot afford to lose even one. This reliability is the only reason Gullick keeps advancing him wages at all.

There is a rumor in the harbor district that Brennan once saved a child from drowning in the deep channel by swimming out into the current with no rope and no life preserver, hauling the boy back to the docks while the other workers stood frozen. He tells people the child was a stranger. The child's mother says he knows the boy's name and visits on birthdays, which he denies with visible embarrassment.

facts.text: She stands at five feet six inches tall with a broad-shouldered, stocky frame, her compact build belying surprising strength in her arms and hands.
Her skin is a muted grey-brown, weathered and calloused from years of labor on the docks, with a faint greenish undertone visible only in certain light.

Her hair is a vivid, fiery red — a conspicuous departure from the dark, coarse hair typical of her heritage — kept in a practical, short-cropped style that she ties back with a leather cord when working.
Her eyes are a striking amber-gold, an unusual trait for a quarter-orc that she inherited from her half-orc mother and that draws unwanted attention in crowded taverns.
Two small, barely visible tusk buds protrude from her lower jaw, each no longer than a quarter inch, a vestigial remnant of her orcish ancestry that she considers an embarrassment.
She grew up in the harbor district of Kethara, the port city where she still lives, the daughter of a half-orc fisherwoman and a Lowlander dock foreman who abandoned the family when she was four.

She has worked as a dockhand since the age of seventeen, loading and unloading cargo from merchant vessels, a grueling job that pays modestly and leaves her with bruised knuckles and aching joints by the end of each day.

She runs an underground dice game out of the back room of a chandler's shop near the eastern pier, operating on a percentage of the pot rather than a fixed buy-in, which she insists is 'more fair' — though her interpretation of fairness excludes anyone who can't pay their debts.

She owes money to at least a dozen people across Kethara, including her landlord, a loan shark named Bellwick, and three separate dock bosses who have each threatened to dock her wages — which they cannot legally do but do anyway.

She is loud, charismatic, and quick to laugh, the kind of person who can talk a stranger into sitting down for a drink within minutes of meeting them, but she has a sharp tongue when cornered and a stubborn streak that makes it nearly impossible for her to ask for help.
